sq.q: \(\text{State the Final Value Theorem for Z-transform.}\)
answer: \(\text{provided the poles of } (z-1)F(z) \text{ are inside the unit circle.}\)

lq.q: a) State and prove the Initial Value Theorem (IVT) and Final Value Theorem (FVT) for the Z-transform. b) Using IVT, find \(x(0)\) and \(x(1)\) for a sequence whose Z-transform is \(X(z) = \frac{z^2 + 2z + 1}{z^2 - 3z + 2}\) . c) Using FVT, find \(\lim_{n \to \infty} x(n)\) if \(X(z) = \frac{0.5z}{z^2 - 1.5z + 0.5}\) , assuming it exists.
answer: a) Theorems: IVT: If \(Z\{x(n)\}=X(z)\) , then \(x(0) = \lim_{z \to \infty} X(z)\) . Proof: \(X(z) = x(0) + x(1)z^{-1} + x(2)z^{-2} + ...\) . As \(z \to \infty\) , all terms with negative powers of z vanish, leaving \(x(0)\) . FVT: If \(Z\{x(n)\}=X(z)\) and all poles of \((z-1)X(z)\) lie inside the unit circle, then \(\lim_{n \to \infty} x(n) = \lim_{z \to 1} (z-1) X(z)\) . Proof: Uses the property \(Z\{x(n+1)-x(n)\} = (z-1)X(z) - z x(0)\) and taking limits as \(z \to 1\) and \(n \to \infty\) under stability conditions.

c) For \(X(z) = \frac{0.5z}{z^2 - 1.5z + 0.5} = \frac{0.5z}{(z-1)(z-0.5)}\) : By FVT: \(\lim_{n \to \infty} x(n) = \lim_{z \to 1} (z-1) X(z) = \lim_{z \to 1} (z-1) \cdot \frac{0.5z}{(z-1)(z-0.5)} = \lim_{z \to 1} \frac{0.5z}{z-0.5} = \frac{0.5(1)}{1-0.5} = 1\) . Note: The pole at z=0.5 is inside |z|=1, and the pole at z=1 is canceled by (z-1) factor, so FVT applicable.
